heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.51 — Duties of registered societies
text:
51. A registered society shall-
(a) have a registered address to which notices and communications shall be sent, and a notice of any change of the address shall be sent to the Registrar;
(b) keep a copy of this Act, Regulations and its by-laws open for perusal free of charge at the registered address of the society; and
(c) maintain a register of its members in a manner as may be prescribed by the Regulations and enter any particulars as prescribed by the Regulations.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.52 — Power to make by-laws
The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.52 — Power to make by-laws
The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.53 — Amendment of by-laws of a registered society
text:
53.–(1) A registered society may, subject to the provisions of this section, amend its by-laws and submit the amendments to the Registrar for registration.
(2) The Registrar shall-
(a) if he is satisfied that, the amendments of the by-laws are not contrary to this Act, register the amendments; or
(b) refuse to register the amendments and notify the society accordingly.
(3) Where the Registrar registers an amendment of the by-laws of a registered society, he shall issue to the society a copy of the amendments certified and sealed by him, and the certified copy which is sealed shall be conclusive evidence of the fact that, the amendments have been duly registered.
(4) An amendment which changes the name of the society shall not affect any right or obligation of the society or any of its members or past members, and any legal proceedings pending may be continued by or against the society under its new name.
(5) An amendment of the by-laws of a registered society shall not be valid until the amendment has been registered under this act.
(6) A society may, within two calendar months from the date of notification by the Registrar of his refusal to register an amendment of any by-laws, appeal to the Commission against the refusal.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.54 — By-laws of a registered society to bind members
text:
54.–(1) The by-laws of a registered society shall, upon registration be binding upon the society and the members thereof to the same extent as if the by-laws were signed by each member of the society and contained covenant by each member to observe the provisions of the by-laws. Amendment of by-laws of a registered society By-laws of a registered society to bind members
(2) A dispute arising out of the interpretation of a by-law of registered society shall be referred to the Registrar.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.55 — Accounts and Audit
text:
55.–(1) A registered society shall, with the approval of the general meeting, employ an Internal Auditor or a number of Internal Auditors as are necessary for the efficient checking of the accounts of the society.
(2) The registered society shall keep proper accounts and other records in relation thereto and within three months prepare in respect of every financial year, a statement of accounts in a form which conforms to the best accounting standards.
(3) The accounts of a registered society except for cooperative banks shall be audited at least once in a year by the corporation or any competent and registered auditor appointed by the general meeting and approved by the Registrar.
(4) The accounts of cooperative banks shall be audited at least once a year by registered auditors appointed by the general meeting and approved by the Registrar upon consultation with the Bank.
(5) An auditor shall submit audited accounts of a cooperative society to members at a general meeting unless the audited accounts have been submitted to the Registrar in a form as may be prescribed.
(6) The Auditor shall submit the audited accounts to a general meeting within four months after the end of the accounting period which include his opinion as to whether or not the affairs of cooperative society have been conducted in accordance with-
(a) the provisions of this Act and, whether the books of accounts kept by the cooperative society are in agreement therewith and give a true and fair view of the state of the affairs of the society; and
(b) the objectives of cooperative society, by-laws and any other resolutions made by the society at a general meeting. Audit
(7) The auditor’s report referred to under subsections
(3) and
(4) shall include an examination of the balance sheet and related income statement and valuation of assets and liabilities of the registered society.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.55 — Accounts and Audit
text:
(8) As soon as the annual accounts of a registered society have been audited, the society shall cause to be submitted to the Registrar, a copy of the audited balance sheet and statement of income and expenditure prepared in respect of that year together with any report made by the auditors thereon.
(9) Where the accounts of a society have been audited and adopted by the general meeting of the society and approved in accordance with subsections
(3) and (4), the accounts shall be conclusive, except as regards any error discovered therein within six months following the date of the approval and except as regards any allegation of fraud, and whenever any error is discovered, within that period the accounts shall forthwith be corrected with the approval of the Registrar and thereafter shall be conclusive.
(10) In the event a society fails to prepare a statement of accounts within a period of three moths in respect of the business of its previous financial year, the members of the relevant Board of the society shall lose their membership of the Board and not be eligible for re-election to the Board for the next six years.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.56 — Registrar may require bank to produce information
text:
56. Notwithstanding anything in any other written law, the Registrar may, where he considers necessary to do so, require any bank-
(a) to furnish any information regarding the transactions of any registered society with the bank;
(b) to produce a copy showing the accounts of the society with the bank from the ledger kept by the bank; and
(c) to produce any cheques paid to the credit of the society or endorsed by the society. require bank to produce information

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.57 — Communication of defects in the operations of registered Society
text:
57.–(1) Where any audit, inquiry or inspection made under this Act discloses any defect in the working of a registered society, the Registrar shall bring the defect to the notice of the society and where the society is affiliated to another registered society, he shall bring the defect to the notice of the other society as well.
(2) The Registrar may, subject to subsection (1), make an order directing the society or its officers to take action as specified in the order and within the time as he may direct in the order as will remedy any defect disclosed in the audit, inquiry or inspection and the society shall forthwith comply without delay.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.58 — Returns to be made by registered societies
text:
58.–(1) A registered society shall submit an annual return to the Registrar.
(2) The Registrar may require a registered society to submit the returns of that society, and prescribe forms in which the returns are to be submitted.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.59 — Defect in the by-laws not to render act of registered society invalid
text: 59. An act of a registered society or a persons purporting to act on behalf of the society in good faith, shall not be deemed to be invalid by reason of the existence of any defect in the by-laws of the registered society or a Board of registered society or in the appointment or election of an officer of the society on the ground that, the officer was disqualified for his appointment.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.60 — Disposal of produce to or through registered society
text:
60.–(1) A registered society which one of its objectives is the disposal of any article which is the produce of agriculture or animal husbandry, shall provide in its by-laws that a member who-
(a) produces any articles has entered into an implied contract to dispose of the whole or any specified amount, proportion or description thereof to or through the society; and of defects in the operations of registered Society Returns to be made by registered societies laws not to render act of registered society invalid Disposal of produce to or through registered society
(b) is proved or adjudged to be guilty of breach of by-laws, shall pay to the society as liquidated damages, a sum ascertained or assessed in a manner as may be prescribed by the by-laws.
(2) A contract implied in the by-laws of a registered society under subsection (1)(a), shall create in favour of the registered society, a first charge upon articles as referred to under subsection (1), whether these articles have been produced or are about to be produced.
(3) In any legal proceedings arising out of a contract implied in the by-laws of a registered society under subsection (1)(a), it shall not be a defence that, the contract is in restraint of trade.
(4) A member of a registered society shall be deemed not to have contravened the by-laws of the society which requires him to deliver any produce to the society, where the failure to deliver the produce to the society was due to the fact that, he had, prior to becoming a member of the society, contracted to deliver the produce to some other person.
(5) A person who applied for membership of a registered society shall, if required so to do, disclose in his application, particulars of contracts made by him for the delivery of any produce to any other person.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.61 — Creation of charge in favour of registered societies
text:
61.–(1) Subject to any prior claim of the government on the property of the debtor and the lien or claim of a landlord in respect of rent or any money recoverable as rent and in the case of immovable property to any prior registered charge thereon-
(a) any rent or outstanding demand payable to a registered society by any member or past member shall be a first charge on the produce of agriculture, animal husbandry, fisheries or any industry and generally the produce of labour and things used in connection with production raised, purchased or produced in whole or in part from any loan whether in money or in goods given to him by the society: Provided that, nothing herein contained shall affect the claim of any bona fide purchaser or transferee without notice; Creation of charge in favour of registered societies
(b) any outstanding demands or dues payable to a registered housing society by any member or past member in respect of rent, shares, loans or purchase money or any other rights or amounts payable to the society shall be first charge upon his interest in the immovable property of the society.
(2) A person shall transfer any property which is subject to a charge under subsection
(1) except with the previous permission in writing of the cooperative society which holds the charge.
(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, any transfer of property made in contravention of the provisions of subsection
(2) shall be void.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.62 — Charges and set-off in respect of share or interest of members
text: 62. A registered society shall have a charge upon the shares or interest in the capital and on the deposit of a member or past member and upon any dividend, bonus, or accumulated funds payable to or due from the member or past member to the society and may set off any sum credited or payable to a member or past member or towards payment of any debt.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.63 — Shares or interest not liable to attachment
text: 63. Subject to the provisions of section 62, the share or interest of a member in the capital of a registered society shall not be liable to attachment or sale under any decree or order of a court in respect of any debt or liability incurred by the member, and the official receiver under the law relating to bankruptcy for the time being in force shall not be entitled to or have any claim on the share or interest.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.64 — Transfer of interest on death of member
text:
64.–(1) On the death or declaration of permanent insanity of a member, a registered society may transfer the share or other interest of the member to the person nominated in accordance with the by-laws of the society or if there is no person nominated, to the person as may appear to the committee to be the heir or legal representative of the member or pay to the nominee, heir or legal representative as the case may be, a sum off in respect of share or interest of members not liable to attachment Transfer of interest on death of member representing the value of the member’s share or interest, as ascertained in accordance with the Regulations or by-laws: Provided that:
(a) in the case of a registered society with unlimited liability, the nominee, heir, or legal representative, may require payment by the society of the value of the shares or interest of the deceased member ascertained as aforesaid; and
(b) in the case of a society with limited liability, the society may transfer the share or interest of the member to the nominee, heir or legal representative, as the case may be, being qualified in accordance with the Regulations and by-laws for membership of the society, or on his application within six months of the date of the death or declaration of permanent insanity, to any person specified in the application who is qualified.
(2) A registered society shall pay other moneys due to the deceased member from the society to the nominee, heir or legal representative, as the case may be.
(3) The transfer and payment made by a registered society in accordance with the provisions of this section shall be valid and effective against any demand made upon the society by any other person.
(4) The Registrar shall be consulted for arbitration in case of misunderstanding between a member and a society under this section.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.65 — Proof of entries in societies’ books
text:
65.–(1) A copy of any entry in a book of a registered society regularly kept in the course of business shall, where certified, in a manner as may be prescribed in the Regulations, be received in any suit or legal proceedings, civil or criminal as prima facie evidence of the existence of the entry and be admitted as evidence of the matters, transactions and accounts therein recorded in every case where and to the same extent as, the original entry is admissible.
(2) An officer of a registered society, in any legal proceedings to which the registered society is not a party shall be compelled societies’ books to produce any of the society’s books, the contents of which can be proved under subsection
(1) or to appear as a witness to prove any matter, transaction or accounts therein recorded unless the court for special reasons directs.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.66 — Exemption from compulsory registration of instruments relating to shares of registered society
text:
66. Subject to the provisions of Part IX, any written law requiring registration of instruments relating to shares and debentures shall not apply to-
(a) any instrument relating to shares in a registered society, notwithstanding that, the assets of the society consist in relation to shares and whole or any part of immovable property;
(b) any endorsement upon or transfer of any debentures issued by any society; or
(c) any debentures issued by the society and not creating, declaring, assigning, limiting or extinguishing any right, title, or interest to or an immovable property except in so far as the instrument whereby the society has mortgaged, conveyed or otherwise transferred the whole or part of its immovable property or any interest therein, to trustees upon trust for the benefit of the holders of debentures.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.67 — Exemption from duty or tax

67.–(1) Notwithstanding the provisions of any law to the contrary, the Minister responsible for finance may, by notice in the Gazette, in the case of any registered society or class of registered societies reduce or remit-
(a) the duty, tax or value added tax which under any laws for the time being in force may be payable in respect of the accumulated funds of the society or the dividends or other payments received by the members of the society on account of the accumulated funds; and
(b) the stamp duty payable under the Stamp Duty Act, on instruments executed by or on behalf of a registered society or by an officer or member and relating to the business of the society of any class of instruments, are respectively chargeable. compulsory instruments relating to shares of registered society duty or tax Cap. 189

(1) shall not be construed as restricting or limiting any power conferred on any authority to grant exemption from any tax, duty, stamp duty, value added tax or fee under any written law.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.68 — Management of registered society
text:
68.–(1) Management of registered society shall be vested in the Board.
(2) Provisions relating to the management of the registered societies shall be as prescribed in the Third Schedule.
(3) The Minister may, in consultation with the Commission, amend or vary the provisions of the Third Schedule.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VII — Duties And Privileges Of Registered Societies › s.69 — Public education and awareness on duties and privileges of societies
text:
69. For the purpose of this Part, a cooperative promotion officer shall-
(a) provide public education and awareness to members of registered societies on the duties and privileges of registered societies; and
(b) the manner in which to access the privileges.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VIII — Revenue And Funds Of Registered Societies › s.70 — Revenue of Registered societies
The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VIII — Revenue And Funds Of Registered Societies › s.71 — Management of revenues and funds of registered societies
text:
71.–(1) A registered society shall, for the purpose of managing its revenues and funds ensure that-
(a) an admission fee is not refundable except in the case where an application for membership has been rejected;
(b) a regular obligatory deposit is made in accordance with the by-laws of the society and is not withdrawn except for purposes and in accordance with conditions specified in the Regulations, or on termination of membership, or for the purposes of securing a loan taken by or a guarantee given by a member, voluntary deposits may be withdrawn subject to any conditions or restriction specified in the by-laws of the registered society;
(c) deposit or loans from persons who are not members of the registered society are subject to the provisions of this Act and the by-laws of the society; and
(d) a share shall not be redeemed except in accordance with the provisions of by-laws of the society where the by-laws allow the redemption and in which case, the said by-laws shall also specify the minimum number of shares a member shall hold while is a member. Management of revenues and funds of registered societies
(2) A society shall not issue bonds or debentures without the authority of the Registrar and in any issue comply with any conditions prescribed by the general meeting.
(3) A registered society which under this Act is required to maintain a reserve fund shall maintain the fund in accordance with the provisions of this Act and by-laws of a registered society.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VIII — Revenue And Funds Of Registered Societies › s.72 — Restriction on loans
text:
72.–(1) A registered society shall not give a loan to any person other than to its member.
(2) A registered society may, with the approval of the Registrar and in accordance with any conditions which the Registrar may prescribe, allow normal business credit to persons to whom goods have been sold or services rendered by the registered bona fide society.
(3) Except with the permission of the Registrar, a society shall not lend money on the security of any movable property other than produce or goods in which the society is authorised to deal.
(4) The Registrar may, by a general or special order, prohibit or restrict the lending of money by any society or class of societies on the security of immovable property.
(5) A registered society whose main object is to supply commodities to its members shall not make any loan nor allow any credit without the sanction of the Registrar who may impose limits on loans or credit as he thinks fit.
(6) A registered society which markets agricultural produce, handicrafts or mineral products of its members may make advances up to a limit not exceeding 75 per centum of the local value as estimated by the committee of agricultural products or handicrafts or mineral products delivered to the society for marketing.
(7) A registered society may with the approval of the general meeting, make loans to another registered body. loans

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VIII — Revenue And Funds Of Registered Societies › s.73 — Restriction on borrowing from non-members
text: 73. A registered society shall receive deposits and loans from persons who are not members to the extent and under the conditions as may be prescribed by the Rules, Regulations or by this Act.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VIII — Revenue And Funds Of Registered Societies › s.74 — Investment of funds
text:
74.–(1) A registered society may invest its funds-
(a) in interest bearing deposit in a cooperative financial institution, or any financial institution as may be approved by the Commission;
(b) in the shares of any other registered society;
(c) in government bonds and other securities; or
(d) in other investments as the Registrar may, with approval of the Commission by order published in the Gazette, declare to be authorised investments for the purpose of this section.
(2) The Commission may advise any registered society to invest its funds or any portion of its funds in any one or more of the investments authorised by or under subsection (1).
(3) Where there is any loss occasioned, in respect of the funds invested, an officer who is a part to the loss commits an offence and on conviction shall be liable to a fine of not less than two million shillings and in addition required to compensate the loss occasioned.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VIII — Revenue And Funds Of Registered Societies › s.75 — Inspection and supervision of cooperative fund
text:
75.–(1) A society shall contribute to a fund established by the Government and be administered by the Commission for the purpose of meeting the expenses of inspection and promotion of cooperative.
(2) The Commission shall prescribe in the Regulations the manner in which the society shall contribute to the fund.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VIII — Revenue And Funds Of Registered Societies › s.76 — Financial provisions
The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VIII — Revenue And Funds Of Registered Societies › s.77 — Dividend and bonus
text:
77.–(1) A society shall not pay a dividend, bonus or distribute any part of its accumulated funds before the balance sheet has been audited by a duly authorised auditor and approved by the general meeting of a relevant cooperative society.
(2) A society with unlimited liability which advances money or goods to any member in excess of the money or the value bonus of the goods deposited by him shall pay a dividend during the period of ten years from the date of its registration.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VIII — Revenue And Funds Of Registered Societies › s.78 — Reserve fund
text:
78.–(1) A society which derives a profit from its transactions shall maintain a reserve fund.
(2) A society with unlimited liability, which advances money or goods to any member in excess of the money or the value of goods deposited by him, shall contribute one fourth of the annual net surplus to the reserve fund and other societies shall contribute a portion or annual net surplus as may be prescribed by the Regulations and by-laws.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VIII — Revenue And Funds Of Registered Societies › s.79 — Distribution of balances
text: 79. Subject to the provisions of this Act and any Regulations made there under, a registered society may apply the annual net balance together with any sum available for distribution from previous years to payment of bonus and any staff incentive bonus scheme in a manner and proportion as may be prescribed by the Regulations or its by-laws.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part VIII — Revenue And Funds Of Registered Societies › s.80 — Contribution for charitable purposes
text:
80.–(1) A registered society may, by resolution in general meeting appropriate from its funds and expend on any charitable, educational or medical purposes or other objects.
(2) A cooperative society shall for the purpose of subsection
(1) establish a special fund to be used in discharging cooperative social responsibilities as may be determined by the society.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part IX — Creation And Registration Of Charges › s.82 — Duty of a society to register charges created by society
text:
82.–(1) It shall be the duty of the registered society to submit to the Registrar, the particulars of a charge created by the society to which section 81 applies, however the registration of any charge may be effected upon the application of any person interested therein.
(2) Where registration is affected on the application of some person other than the society, the person shall be entitled to recover from the society, the amount of any fees properly paid by him to the Registrar on registration.
(3) Where a registered society defaults in submitting to the Registrar the particulars of any charge created by the society for registration to which section 81 applies, unless the registration has been effected by some other person, the society and an officer thereof who knowingly took part in the default on conviction shall be liable to a fine of not less than one hundred thousand shillings for every day during which the default continues. to register charges created by society

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part IX — Creation And Registration Of Charges › s.83 — Duty of a society to register charges on property acquired
text:
83.–(1) Where a registered society acquires any property which is subject to a charge to which section 81 would apply if the charge had been created by the society after the acquisition of the property, the society shall cause the prescribed particulars of the charge together with a certified copy of the instrument if any, by which the charge was created or is evidenced, to be delivered to the Registrar for registration within forty-five days after the date of which the acquisition is completed.
(2) Where the default is made in complying with the provisions of this section, the society and an officer thereof who is knowingly a party to the default, commits an offence and on conviction shall be liable to a fine of not less than one hundred thousand shillings for every day during which the default continues.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part IX — Creation And Registration Of Charges › s.84 — Register of charges
text:
84.–(1) The Registrar shall keep, with respect to each registered society, a register in the prescribed form, of charges requiring registration under the provisions of this Part, and on payment of the prescribed fee, enter in the register with respect to any charge the following particulars-
(a) in the case of a charge to the benefit of which the holders of a series of debentures are entitled,the particulars as are specified in subsection
(6) of section 81;
(b) in the case of a charge to the benefit of which the holders of a series of debentures are entitled, the particulars as are specified in subsection
(6) of section 82; and
(c) in the case of any other charge-
(i) if the charge is a charge created by the society. the date of its creation, and if the charge was a charge existing on the property acquired by the society, the date of the acquisition of the property;
(ii) the amount secured by the charge;
(iii) short particulars of the report charged; and
(iv) the persons entitled to the charge.
(2) The Registrar shall issue a certificate of registration of any charge registered in pursuance of the provisions of this Part, stating the amount thereby secured, and the certificate to register charges on property acquired Register of charges shall be conclusive evidence that, the requirements of this Part as to registration have been complied with.
(3) The register kept in pursuance of this section shall be open to inspection by any person on payment of the prescribed fee as may be determined by the Registrar.
(4) The Registrar shall keep a chronological index in the prescribed form and containing the prescribed particular of the charges entered in the register.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part IX — Creation And Registration Of Charges › s.85 — Endorsement of certificate of registration of debentures
text:
85.–(1) A registered society shall cause a copy of a certificate of registration given under section 84 to be endorsed on a debenture or certificate of debenture stock which is issued by the society, and the payment of which is secured by the charge registered: Provided that, this subsection shall not be construed as requiring a society to cause a certificate of registration of any charge given to be endorsed on any debenture or certificate of debenture stock issued by the society before the charge was created.
(2) Where a person knowingly and willfully authorises or permits the delivery of any debenture or certificate of debenture stock which under the provisions of this section is required to have been endorsed on it, a copy of a certificate of registration without the copy being endorsed on it, commits an offence and without prejudice to any other liability, on conviction shall be liable to a fine of not less than one million shillings.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part IX — Creation And Registration Of Charges › s.86 — Entry of satisfaction and rectification of register
text:
86.–(1) The Registrar upon satisfaction that-
(a) the debt for which any registered charge was given has been paid or satisfied; and
(b) a memorandum of satisfaction be entered on the register, may furnish to the society the copy of the memorandum of satisfaction.
(2) The Registrar, on being satisfied that, the omission to register a charge within the time required by this Part, or the omission or misstatement of any particular matter with Endorsement of certificate of debentures Entry of satisfaction and rectification of register respect to any charge or in a memorandum of satisfaction was accidental or due to in advertence or some other sufficient cause, or is not of a nature to prejudice the position of creditors or members of the society or on other grounds, it is just and equitable to grant relief may, on the application of the registered society or any person interested and in terms and conditions as seen to him just and expedient, order that, the time for registration be extended or, as the case may be, that the omission or misstatement be rectified.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part IX — Creation And Registration Of Charges › s.87 — Enforcement of security
text:
87.–(1) Where a person obtains an order for the appointment of a receiver or manager of the property of a registered society or appoints a receiver or manager under any power contained in any instrument, he shall, within seven days from the date of the order or the appointment under the said powers, give notice or the facts to the Registrar and the Registrar shall, on payment of the prescribed fee, enter the facts in the register of charges.
(2) Where a person is appointed as a receiver or manager of the property of a registered society under the powers contained in any instrument ceases to act as the receiver or manager, he shall on ceasing, give the Registrar notice to that effect, and the Registrar shall enter the notice in the register of charges.
(3) A person who defaults in complying with any of the requirements of this section commits an offence and on conviction shall be liable to a fine not exceeding five thousand shillings for every day during which the default continues.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part IX — Creation And Registration Of Charges › s.88 — Copies of instrument creating charges to be kept by society
text:
88.–(1) A registered society shall cause to be kept at the registered address of the society, a copy of an instrument creating any charge requiring to be registered under the provisions of this Part.
(2) Where a registered society fails to comply with the provisions of subsection (1), the society and an officer thereof who is knowingly a party to the default on conviction shall be liable to a fine of not less than one hundred thousand shillings for every day during which the default continues. security Copies of instrument creating charges to be kept by society

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part IX — Creation And Registration Of Charges › s.89 — Society’s register of charges
text:
89.–(1) A registered society shall keep at registered address of the society, a register of charges and enter therein charges specifically charges effecting property of the society and floating charges on the property or assets of the society giving in each case, a short description of the property charged, the amount of the charge and the names of the persons entitled thereto.
(2) Where an officer of the society knowingly and willfully authorises or permits the omission of any entry required to be made in pursuance of this section in any register commits an offence and on conviction shall be liable to a fine of not less than five million shillings.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part IX — Creation And Registration Of Charges › s.90 — Right to inspect copies of instruments creating mortgage, charges and society’s register of charges
text:
90.–(1) The copies of the instrument creating any charge required to be registered with the Registrar under the provisions of this Part and the registered society in pursuance of section 84, shall be open during business hours, subject to a reasonable meeting restrictions as the society in general meeting may impose for the inspection of any creditor or members of the society without fee, and the register of charges shall be open to inspection of any person on payment of fee as may be determined by the general meeting.
(2) Where inspection of the copies or register is refused, an officer of the society refusing inspection or who knowingly and willfully permits the refusals, commits an offence and on conviction shall be liable to a fine of not less than five hundred thousand shillings for every day during which the refusal continues and any court may by order, compel an immediate inspection of the copies or register.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part X — Inspection Of Affairs Of Cooperative Societies › s.91 — Inquiry by Registrar officers as inspectors
text:
91.–(1) The Registrar may, on his own motion or on the application of the majority of the members of the Board of not less than one-third, direct and authorise some persons of charges copies of instruments creating mortgage, charges and society’s Inquiry by Registrar officers as inspectors in writing to hold an inquiry into the by-laws, activities and financial affairs of the registered society.
(2) The officers and members of the society shall produce books and documents of the society and furnish informations in regard to the affairs of the society, as the person authorised by the Registrar may require.
(3) The general meeting may decide to held an enquiry into the affairs of their registered society.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part X — Inspection Of Affairs Of Cooperative Societies › s.92 — Designation of cooperative officer as cooperative inspectors
text:
92.–(1) The Commission may, by order published in the Gazette, designate by name, a cooperative officer who shall perform the function of inspection of cooperative societies.
(2) The cooperative officers designated under subsection
(1) shall be accountable to the Registrar.
(3) A cooperative inspector shall prepare and submit to the Registrar a report of registered cooperative society inspected and with regard to any other matters as the Registrar may require him to report upon.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part X — Inspection Of Affairs Of Cooperative Societies › s.93 — Inspection
text:
93.–(1) The Registrar shall make or cause to be made a continuous inspection on the by-laws, activities and financial affairs of a registered society.
(2) Without prejudice to the generality of subsection (1), the Registrar shall, on the application of a creditor of a registered society, inspect or direct some person authorised by him by order in writing in his behalf to inspect the books of the society: Provided that, an inspection under this subsection shall not be carried out or directed unless-
(a) the creditor satisfies the Registrar that, the debt is a sum then due, and he has demanded payment thereof and has not received satisfactory explanation within a reasonable time; and
(b) the creditor deposits with the Registrar sum as security for costs for the purposes of inspection as the Registrar may require.
(3) The Registrar shall communicate the results of any inspection carried out under subsection
(2) to the creditor. Designation of cooperative officer as cooperative inspectors

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part X — Inspection Of Affairs Of Cooperative Societies › s.94 — Cost of inquiry
text:
94.–(1) Where an inquiry is held under section 91 or an inspection is made under section 93, the Registrar may, by a certificate under his hand and seal, make an award apportioning the costs, or part of the costs as he may think right, between the society, the members or creditor demanding an inquiry or inspection and the officer or former officers of the society.
(2) The Registrar may lodge a certified copy of a certificate issued by him under subsection
(1) in a court of a Resident Magistrate or a District Court and upon being lodged, the certificate shall be deemed to be a decree passed by the court for the payment by the person named in the certificate to the Registrar of the sum specified in the certificate and the sum may be recovered in any manner prescribed by the Civil Procedure Code for the enforcement of decrees and the provisions of that Act relating to executions of decrees shall apply, mutatis mutandis, to proceedings for the recovery of costs awarded under this Act.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part X — Inspection Of Affairs Of Cooperative Societies › s.95 — Surcharge
text:
95.–(1) Where upon an inquiry under section 91 or upon an inspection under section 93 or upon audit under section 55, the Registrar is satisfied that, a past or present officer or member has made or authorised an unlawful payment or has by negligence or misconduct caused a deficiency or a loss or failure to bring to account or has by negligence or misconduct caused loss of or damage to any property of a registered society, the Registrar shall surcharge the person with the unlawful payment, deficiency or loss, or the sum which ought to have been brought to account or the value of the property lost or damaged or portion of unlawful payment, deficiency, loss, sum, value or cost as the Registrar may consider reasonable having regard to the circumstances of the case.
(2) The Registrar shall give notice in writing to a person surcharged under subsection
(1) of the amount surcharged and the ground upon which the surcharge is made, and a person aggrieved by the decision of the Registrar may, not later than thirty days from the receipt of the notice, appeal to the Minister. Cap. 33
(3) Where a person surcharged-
(a) fails to pay the amount within thirty days after the service of the notice upon him in accordance with subsection (2); or
(b) has appealed to the Minister and fails to pay the amount of the surcharge, if any, decided upon by the Minister within fifteen days from the date of the decision of the Minister, the Registrar shall issue a certificate under his hand and seal specifying the name and address of the person who has been surcharged and the amount of the surcharge and the certificate or a certified copy thereof shall be lodged in a court of Resident Magistrate or a District Court.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XI — Amalgamation And Division Of Cooperative Societies › s.96 — Amalgamation
text:
96.–(l) Two or more registered societies may resolve, by a resolution approved at a general meeting of the societies at which not less than two-thirds of the members or delegates of the society are present and held after reasonable notice given of the place and time of the meeting and the intention to move the resolution thereto, to amalgamate as a single society. Cap. 33
(2) Where the Registrar is satisfied that-
(a) two or more registered societies have resolved to amalgamate as a single society in accordance with the provisions of subsection (l);
(b) the proposed by-laws of the proposed amalgamated society are unobjectionable; and
(c) the proposed amalgamation is not against the interest of the members of the societies proposing to amalgamate or against public interest, he may, by order published in the Gazette, amalgamate the societies.
(3) An order made under subsection (2), shall specify-
(a) the date on which the societies shall amalgamate; and
(b) the name of the amalgamating society and may contain directions as the Registrar may consider necessary for the purpose of giving effect to the amalgamation or safeguarding the interests of any person.
(4) Where an order is made under subsection (2)-
(a) the assets and liabilities of the amalgamating societies shall, by virtue of an order and without further assurance, vest in the amalgamated society;
(b) the Registrar shall cancel the registration of the amalgamating societies and the cancellation shall be effective as from the effective date; and
(c) the Registrar shall, notwithstanding the provisions of sections 30 and 31, register the amalgamated society and the by-laws of the amalgamated society.
(5) Notwithstanding subsection (1), the Registrar may, by notice in writing, advise two or more societies to amalgamate where he is satisfied that, it is in the interest of the societies or public to do so.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XI — Amalgamation And Division Of Cooperative Societies › s.97 — Defects or irregularity in the notice
text: 97. An amalgamation of registered societies or division of a registered society shall not be invalid by reason of defect or irregularity in any notice or order required to be given or made under this Part.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XI — Amalgamation And Division Of Cooperative Societies › s.98 — Division of societies
text:
98.–(1) An existing registered society may resolve by a resolution approved at a general meeting at which not less than two-thirds of the members or delegates of the society are present and held after reasonable notice given of the place and time of the meeting and the intention to move the resolution thereat, to divide itself into two or more proposed new societies.
(2) A resolution passed under subsection
(1) shall contain proposals for the division of the assets and liabilities of the society among the proposed new societies, and may prescribe the area of operation of, and specify the members who shall constitute each of the proposed new societies.
(3) The Registrar may by notice in writing advise on voluntary division, where is satisfied that-
(a) an existing society has resolved to divide itself into two or more new societies in accordance with subsection (1);
(b) the resolution complies with the provisions of subsection (2);
(c) the proposed new societies shall be economically viable when registered; and
(d) the proposed division is not against the interests of the members of the existing society or the public.
(4) The Registrar may, by Order published in the Gazette, divide the existing society which has voluntarily passed the resolution for division under subsection (1).
(5) An order made under subsection
(4) shall specify-
(a) the date on which the existing society shall be divided into the new societies;
(b) the name of the existing society and the names of the new societies into which it is divided;
(c) the manner in which the assets and liabilities of the existing society shall be divided among the new societies; Defects or irregularity in the notice Division of societies
(d) where necessary, the area of operation of each of the new societies; and
(e) other directions as the Registrar may consider necessary for the purpose of giving effect to the division or safeguarding the interests of any person.

text:
(6) Where an order is made under subsection (4)-
(a) the assets and liabilities of the existing society subsisting on the effective date shall, by virtue of an order and without further assurance, vest in the new societies in the manner specified in the order;
(b) the Registrar shall cancel the registration of the existing society and the cancellation shall be effective as from the effective date; and
(c) the Registrar shall, notwithstanding the provisions of sections 30 and 31, register the new societies and their respective by-laws: Provided that, where the society does not agree with the advice of the Registrar on division, he may dissolve that society under section 99.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.99 — Dissolution
text: 99. Where the Registrar after an inquiry has been held under section 91 or an inspection has been made under section 93 or on receipt of an application made by three-fourths of the members of a registered society or failure to comply with the provisions of sections 96 and 98, is of the opinion that, the society ought to be dissolved he may, by order in writing and after notifying the general meeting of the federation if any, cancel the registration of the society.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.100 — Cancellation of registration of society
text:
100.–(1) Where it is a condition of the registration of a society that, it should consist of at least a required minimum members, the Registrar may, by order in writing, cancel the registration of the society, where it is proved to his satisfaction that, the society number of the members has been reduced to less than the required minimum as per section 20.
(2) Where the Registrar has reasonable cause to believe that, a registered society has not commenced its business within six months of registration, or has ceased to carry on business, he may, after the expiry of three months from the date of publishing a notice to that effect in the Gazette, by order in writing, cancel the registration of the society and the cancellation shall be Gazetted.
(3) The Registrar shall cancel the registration of any savings and credit societies that fail to comply with the requirement to present audited accounts as required by section 47 of the Bank of Tanzania Act, unless sufficient evidence is given to the effect that, any savings and credit societies have established a technical and financial assistance linkage with a professionally managed financial services institution or program.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.101 — Appeal against cancellation of registration
text:
101.–(1) Where the registration of a society is cancelled under the provisions of section 100, a member of the society of which the registration is cancelled may, within thirty days from the date of the order canceling the registration, appeal against the order to the Minister.
(2) Where an appeal is presented within thirty days from the making of an order canceling the registration of a society, the order shall take effect on the expiry of that period.
(3) Where an appeal is presented within thirty days, the order shall not take effect until it is confirmed by the Minister.
(4) Where an appeal has been presented within thirty days, the Minister may proceed to consider the same and confirm the order notwithstanding that, thirty days have not elapsed, and an order is confirmed, a further appeal shall not be allowed against the order.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.102 — Effect of cancellation of registration
text:
102.–(1) Where the registration of a society is cancelled, the cancellation shall take effect and except for the purposes of the winding up of its affairs, the society shall cease to exist as a Cap. 197 Effect of corporate body from the date when the order of cancellation takes effect.
(2) Where the Registrar cancels the registration of a society under any of the provisions of this Act, he shall make an order as he may deem fit respecting the custody of the books and documents and for the protection of the assets of the society until the order canceling the registration of the society takes effect.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.103 — Winding up
text:
103.–(1) Where the registration of a society is cancelled under section 100 or the registered society is dissolved under section 99, the Registrar shall-
(a) appoint by order in writing, a custodian of assets and liabilities of the society immediately after cancellation is effected; and
(b) within forty days, appoint a competent person or persons to be liquidator of the society’s assets and liabilities.
(2) The names of the persons appointed under subsection
(1) shall be published in the Gazette.
(3) The Registrar shall specify the period limit within which the liquidation process shall be finalised.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.104 — Power of liquidator
The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.105 — Power of Registrar to control liquidation
The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.106 — Power to stay or restrain proceedings against society
text: 106. At any time after the cancellation of a registered society takes effect, the liquidator, or any creditor member of the society, may, where any suit or proceedings against the society is pending in any court, apply to the court in which the suit or proceedings is pending for a stay of proceedings therein and the court to which the application is made, may stay the proceedings accordingly on the terms as it thinks fit.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.107 — Avoidance of disposition of property after cancellation
text: 107. A disposition of the property including things in action of a registered society and any transfer of shares or alteration in the status of the members of the society made after the cancellation of the registered society takes effect shall, unless the disposition, transfer or alteration after is made by the liquidator, be void.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.108 — Avoidance of attachment
text: 108. Where the registration of a society is cancelled, any attachment, distress or execution put in force against the assets of the society after the cancellation takes effect, shall be void.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.109 — Power of Registrar to assess damage
text:
109.–(1) Where in the case of the winding up of a society, it appears that, a person who has taken part in the organisation or management of the society or any past or present chairman, secretary, member of the Board or other officer of the society or restrain proceedings against society disposition of property after attachment Power of Registrar to assess damage has disapplied or retained or become liable or accountable for any money or property of the society or has been guilty of misfeance or breach of trust in relation to the society, the Registrar may, on the application of the liquidator or of any creditor or contributor, investigate the conduct of the person and make an order requiring him to repay or restore the money or property or any part thereof as the case may be, with interest at the rate as the Registrar thinks just or contribute the sum to the assets of the society by way of compensation in regard to the misapplication, retainer, misfeance or breach of trust as the Registrar thinks just.
(2) Subject to subsection (1), the aggrieved person may appeal to the Commission within twenty one days.
(3) Where the Registrar has ordered payment of any money or delivery of any property under subsection (1), the money or property may be recovered on production of an order to the District Court or the Court of a Resident Magistrate having jurisdiction over the person from whom the money or property is claimable in the same manner as if the order were the decree of the Court.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.110 — Power to arrest absconding promoter
text:
110.–(1) A Court of a Resident Magistrate may, on the, application of the Registrar or of the liquidator and on proof of probable cause of the absconding of a promoter and upon believing that, the promoter is about to quit the United Republic of Tanzania or otherwise to abscond or remove any of his property for the purpose of evading calls or avoiding investigation of his conduct or examination by the liquidator or by the Registrar respecting the affairs of the society or compliance with any order made by the Registrar under subsection
(1) of section l09, cause him to be arrested, and his books and papers and movable or immovable property to be detained until the time as the court may order.
(2) For the purpose of this section: “promoter” means a founder member of a cooperative society. absconding promoter

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.111 — Debts of description may be proved
text: 111. In a winding up of a registered society, the debts payable on a contingency, and claims against the society present or future, certain or contingent, ascertained or sounding in damages, shall be admissible to proof against the society, a just estimate being made so far as possible or the value of the debts or claims as may be subject to any contingency or sound in damages or for some other reason do not bear a certain value.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.112 — Where society is insolvent
text: 112. In the winding up of a registered society which is insolvent, the procedure under the Bankruptcy Act with regard to the respective insolvent rights of secured and unsecured creditors and debts provable and the valuation of annuities and future and contingent liabilities shall apply with respect to the estates of persons adjudged bankrupt, and persons who in any case would be entitled to prove for and realise dividends out of the assets of the society, may come in under the winding up on and make claims against the society as they respectively are entitled to by virtue of this section.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.113 — Preferable payments
text:
113.–(1) In the winding up of a registered society, there shall be paid payments in priority to other debts-
(a) government taxes and local rates due from the society at the re1evant date and having become due and payable within twelve months next before the date not exceeding in the whole one year’s assessment;
(b) government rents not more than one year in arrears;
(c) wages or salary of services rendered to the society during four months next before the relevant date and wages of any workman or labourer in respect of services rendered; and
(d) amounts due in respect of any compensation under any law for the time being in force in Tanzania relating to compensation of workman, being amounts which have accrued before the relevant date, unless the society has, immediately prior to the relevant date, under any contract with insurers, rights capable of being transferred to and vested in the workman. Debts of description may be proved insolvent Cap. 25 Preferable payments
(2) Notwithstanding anything in paragraph
(c) of subsection (1), the sum to which priority is to be given under that paragraph shall not in the case of one claimant exceed one hundred thousand shillings.
(3) Where a claimant under paragraph
(c) of subsection (1), is a labourer in husbandry who has entered into contract for the payment of a portion of his wages in a lump sum at the end of the year of hiring, he shall have priority in respect of the whole of the sum, a part thereof, as liquidator may decide to be due under the contract, proportionate to the time of service up to the relevant date.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.113 — Preferable payments
text:
(4) Where a compensation under any law for the time being in force in Tanzania relating to compensation of workmen is a weekly payment, the amount due in respect thereof shall for the purpose of paragraph
(d) of subsection (1), be taken to be the amount of the lump sum for which the weekly payment could, if redeemable, be redeemed if the employer made an application for that purpose under the law.
(5) Where a payment has been made to any clerk, servant, workman or labourer in the employment of the society on account of wages or salary out of money advanced by some person for that purpose, the person by whom the money was advanced shall in a winding up have a right of priority in respect of the money advanced and paid up to the amount by which the sum in respect of which the clerk, servant, workman or labourer, would have been entitled to priority if the winding up has been diminished by a reason of the payment having been made.
(6) The debts referred to in subsection
(1) shall-
(a) rank equally among themselves and be paid in full unless the assets are insufficient to meet them in which case, they shall abate in equal proportions; and
(b) so far as the assets of the society available for payment of general creditors are insufficient to meet them, have priority over the claims of holders of debentures under any floating charge created by society, and be paid accordingly out of any property comprised in or subject to that charge.
(7) For the purposes of this section-
(a) a remuneration in respect of a period of absence from work through sickness or other good cause shall be deemed to be wages in respect of services rendered to the society during the period; and
(b) the expression “relevant date” means the date on which the cancellation of the registration of the society takes effects.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.114 — Fraudulent preference
text:
114.–(1) A transfer, conveyance, mortgage, charge, delivery of good, payment, execution or other act relating to property made or done by or against a registered society within six months before the date on which the cancellation of its registration takes effect which had it been made or done by or against an individual within six months before presentation of bankruptcy petition on which he is adjudged bankrupt, would be deemed in his bankruptcy a fraudulent preference, shall in the event of the society being wound up be deemed fraudulent preference of its creditors and be void accordingly.
(2) A transfer, conveyance or assignment by a society of its property to trustees for the benefit of its creditors shall, if done under the circumstance stipulated under subsection (1), be void to its intents.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.115 — Liabilities and obligation of fraudulent preference
text:
115.–(1) Where anything made or done is void under section 114 as a fraudulent preference of a person interested in property mortgaged or charted to secure the society’s debt then without prejudice to any rights or liabilities arising apart from this provision the preferred persons shall be subject to the same liabilities, and have the same rights, as if he had undertaken to be personally liable as surety for the debt to the extent of the mortgage or charge on the property or the value of his interest, whichever is the less.
(2) The value of the said person’s interest shall be determined as at the date of the transaction constituting the fraudulent Fraudulent preference fraudulent preference preference, and determined as if the interest were free of encumbrances other than those to which the mortgage or charge for the society’s debt was the subject.
(3) On an application made to the liquidator with respect to any payment on the ground that, the payment was a fraudulent preference of a surety or guarantor, the liquidator shall have jurisdiction to determine any questions with respect to the payment arising between the person to whom the payment was made and the surety or guarantor and grant relief in respect thereof, notwithstanding that, it is not necessary so to do for the purpose of the winding up.
(4) The provisions of subsection
(3) shall apply, with the necessary modifications, in relation to transactions other than the payment of money as it applies in relation to the payments.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.116 — Effecting of floating charge
text: 116. Where a registered society is being wound up, a floating charge on the undertaking or property of the society created within six months of the cancellation of the registration of the society taking effect shall, unless it is proved that, the society immediately after the creation of the charge, was solvent, be invalid, except to the amount of any cash paid to the society at the time of or subsequently the creation of, and in consideration for the charge, together with interest on that amount at the rate of six percent per annum or other rate as may be prescribed.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.117 — Disclaimer of property in case of society wound up
text:
117.–(1) Where any part of the property of a registered society which is being wound up consists of land of any tenure burdened with onerous case of covenants of shares or stock in companies of profitable contracts or any property that is un saleable or not readily saleable by reason of its binding the possessor thereof to the performance of any onerous act or to payment of any sum of money, the liquidator, notwithstanding that he has endeavored to sell or has taken possession of the property or exercised any act of ownership in relation thereto, may, with the leave of the Registrar and subject to the provisions of this section, by writing signed by him, at any time within twelve months after the cancellation of the registration of the floating charge property in case of society wound up society taking effect or extended period as may be allowed by the Registrar, disclaim the property.
(2) The disclaimer shall operate to determine, as from the fate of disclaimer, the rights, interest and liabilities of the society in or in respect of the property disclaimed but shall not, except so far as is necessary for the purpose of releasing the society and the property of the society from liabilities of any other person affect the rights or the liabilities of any person.
(3) The Registrar before or on granting leave to disclaim, may require the notices to be given to persons interested, and impose terms as a condition of granting leave, and make other order in the matter as he thinks just.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.117 — Disclaimer of property in case of society wound up
text:
(4) The liquidator shall not be entitled to disclaim any property under this section in any case, where an application in writing has been made to him by any person interested in the property requiring him to decide whether he will or will not disclaim and the liquidator has not, within a period of twenty eight days after the receipt of the application or further period as may be allowed by the Registrar, give notice to the applicant that, he intends to apply for leave to disclaim, and, in the case of a contract, if the liquidator, after an application or further period as may be allowed by the Registrar, give notice to the applicant that, he intends to apply for leave to disclaim, and, in the case of a contract, if the liquidator, after an application as aforesaid, does not within the said period or further period disclaim the contract, he shall be deemed to have adopted it.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.118 — Restriction of rights of creditor in case of society being wound up
text:
118.–(1) Where a creditor has issued execution against the movable or immovable property of registered society or has attached any debt creditor as due to the society, and the society is subsequently wound up, he shall not be entitled to retain the benefit of the execution or attachment against the liquidator in the winding up of the society unless he has completed rights of creditor in case of society being wound up the execution or attachment before the date on which the cancellation of the registration of the society take effect: Provided that-
(a) a person who purchases in good faith under a sale by bailiff on an order of a court any movable property of a society of which an execution has been levied shall acquire a good title thereto against the liquidator; and
(b) the rights conferred by this subsection on the liquidator may be set aside by the Registrar in favour of the creditor to the extent and subject to the terms as the Registrar may think fit.
(2) For the purpose of this section, the execution against movable property shall be taken to be completed by seizure and sale, and an attachment of a debt shall be deemed to be completed by receipt of the debt, and an execution against immovable property shall be deemed to be completed by seizure and, in the case of an equitable interest, by the appointment of a receiver.
(3) The right conferred upon the liquidator by this section may be enforced by him by a civil suit in any court of competent jurisdiction.
(4) In this Part, the expression “movable property” includes chattels personal, and the expression “bailiff” includes any officer charged with the execution of a writ or other process.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.119 — Duties of court in execution
text:
119.–(1) Where a movable property of a registered society is taken in execution and, before the sale thereof or the completion of the execution by receipt of recovery of the full amount of the levy, notice is served taken in execution upon the court which issued the execution that, the registration of the society has been cancelled, the court shall require the bailiff to deliver the movable property including any money seized or received in part satisfaction of the execution to the liquidator and the bailiff shall forth-with comply with the requirement.
(2) Where the bailiff on being required by the court under subsection (1), delivers the movable property including the money, if any, seized or received by him, the costs of execution the execution shall be a first charge on the goods or money delivered and the liquidator may sell the goods, or a sufficient part thereof, for the purpose of satisfying the charge.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.120 — Preservation of books and records
text: 120. On the completion of the duties under section 119, the liquidator shall hand over to the Registrar the books and records of the society, and the Registrar may after the period of two years from the date of removal of the name of the society from the register cause the books and records to be preserved in an archive.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XII — Dissolution Of Cooperative Societies › s.121 — Court not to have jurisdiction in dissolution of societies
text: 121. Save so far as is expressly provided for in this Act, a court shall not have any jurisdiction in respect of any matter connected with the dissolution of a registered society.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XIII — Financial Provisions › s.124 — Accounting and audit
text:
124.–(1) The Commission shall cause to be kept and maintained in accordance with the International Accounting Standards, proper books of accounts with respect to-
(a) sums of moneys received and expended;
(b) the assets and liabilities of the Commission; and
(c) the income and expenditure statement of the Commission.
(2) Within six months of the close of every financial year, the Controller and Auditor-General in accordance with the Public Audit Act shall audit the accounts including the balance sheet of the Commission.
(3) An income and expenditure accounts and audited balance sheet shall be placed before a meeting of the Commission and, if adopted, it shall be endorsed with a certificate to that effect.
(4) As soon as the accounts of the Commission have been audited, and in any case not later than six months after the close of the financial year, the Commission shall submit to the Minister a copy of the audited statement of accounts together with a copy of the report on that statement made by the auditors.
(5) The Minister shall, as soon as practicable after receiving the report, lay before the National Assembly the audited accounts.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XIII — Financial Provisions › s.125 — Financial year
text: 125. The financial year of the Commission shall be the period of twelve months beginning from 1st day of July and ending at 30th day of June of the following year.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XIV — Offences › s.126 — Offences
The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XIV — Offences › s.127 — Offences by body corporate firm
text:
127.–(1) A act which if done by an individual would be an offence against this Act or regulations or orders made under this Act shall, if done by a body corporate, be an offence by a Director and Secretary thereof unless he proves that, the offence was committed without his consent or connivance and he exercised due diligence to prevent the commission of the offence as the ought to have been exercised having regard to the nature of his functions in that capacity and the circumstances.
(2) Where an offence against this Act or any regulations or orders made under this Act has been committed by a partner corporate firm in a firm, a person who at the time of the commission of the offence was a partner in that firm, or was purporting to act in that capacity, shall be deemed to have committed the offence, unless he proves that, the offence was committed without his consent or connivance and he exercised due diligence to prevent the commission of the offence as he ought to have exercised having regard to the nature of his functions in that capacity and the circumstances.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XIV — Offences › s.128 — Offences by agents
text: 128. Where an offence under this Act or any subsidiary legislation made under it is committed by a person as an agent or employee, the agent or employee, the principal or employer, commits an offence and on conviction shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly unless he proves to the satisfaction of the court that, he had no knowledge and could not by the exercise of reasonable diligence have had knowledge of the commission of the offence.

heading_path: The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XIV — Offences › s.129 — Penalty for soliciting violation of contracts
text:
129.–(1) A person, firm or company having knowledge or notice of the existence of a registered society which has one of its objects, the disposal of any article as part of its business, who solicits or persuades or contracts any person to sell or deliver goods as service in violation of the by-laws of that cooperative society, on conviction shall be liable to a fine of not less than five million shillings for a person and not less than ten million shillings for a firm or company for each offence, and in addition pay to the society concerned the market price of the goods or service as the case may be, at the date of the commission of the offence.
(2) A person, firm or company as aforesaid shall be deemed to have knowledge or notice of the existence of cooperative society, where the said society has notified the existence of the cooperative society and the relevant by-laws thereof in the Gazette or a registered society which has one of its objects, the disposal of any article which is the product of agriculture or animal husbandry, in any newspaper circulating in Tanzania. The Cooperative Societies Act, Cap. 211 (R.E. 2023) › Part XIV — Offences › s.131 — Prohibition of use of the word “Cooperative”
text:
131.–(1) A person other than a registered society shall not trade or carry on business under any name or title of which the word “Cooperative” or the word “Co-operative” its equivalent in any other language is part without the sanction of the Commission.
(2) A person other than a bona fide savings and credit society shall not trade or carry on business under any name or title of which the words “Saving and Credit Society” or their equivalent in any other language is part without the sanction of the Commission.
(3) A person who contravenes any of the provisions of this section, commits an offence and on conviction shall be liable to a fine of not less than two million shillings and in the case of a continuing offence, to further fine of one hundred thousand shillings for each day on which the offence is continued after conviction thereof.
